cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What is a retry escalation ladder?
cards.answer: A failure policy for agent loops where each further attempt on a stalled task changes strategy instead of repeating the previous prompt — successive rungs widen context, permitted changes, and cost; a stall counter decides when to climb; a terminal rung ends the task.

cards.heading: Why not just retry the same prompt
cards.question: Why does re-issuing an identical prompt on an already-failed task waste tokens?
cards.answer: It re-samples the same distribution the first attempt already failed against, so it spends tokens to buy mostly the same answer instead of a genuinely different attempt.

cards.heading: Three-rung example
cards.question: What are the three rungs in the worked example of a retry escalation ladder?
cards.answer: A standard prompt (fix it without changing behaviour); a retry prompt that includes the previous attempt's (truncated) output and instructs a different approach; and an exploration prompt that lifts the blast-radius constraint, letting the agent refactor surrounding code and pull in neighbouring files.

cards.heading: When to escalate
cards.question: What decides when a stalled unit climbs to the next rung of the ladder?
cards.answer: A per-unit stall counter tracking consecutive rounds with no improvement, not a fixed round number — so cheap attempts aren't abandoned prematurely and expensive ones aren't wasted on units still progressing.

cards.heading: Terminal rung
cards.question: What happens at the top rung of a retry escalation ladder once it fails?
cards.answer: The unit is dropped from the queue and surfaced for a human, rather than retried again — this is what bounds the loop and stops it being unbounded.
